evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, received 欠部 text
evidence.text: The entry defines 歌 as ‘詠也’ and analyzes it as 从欠哥聲. In the same section 欠 is explained as an open mouth with breath rising out. The received dictionary therefore assigns 欠 a semantic-classifier role and 哥 a phonetic role; this is an analysis of the received form, not direct evidence for the earliest graph.
evidence.title: 說文解字/08 - 維基文庫

evidence.text: The collation reports a late Spring-and-Autumn bronze form from 余贎兒鐘 (集成184), an early Warring States form, Chu manuscript evidence, received Shuowen forms and Qin Shuihudi slip evidence. Its prose analyzes the bronze form as 言+可 and later forms as 欠+哥, with a 言+哥 variant. It is a secondary compilation: the reported forms suggest a change in written structure, but do not establish a continuous ancestry or explain whether the forms represent chronological replacement, regional variants, or related spellings.
evidence.title: 歌字形演变字源_汉字「歌」

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, 可部 entry 哥, online text with Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The received entry says ‘哥，聲也。从二可。古文以爲謌字.’ Duan Yucai comments that the sense ‘sound’ was not then attested in use and that Han texts often used 哥 for 歌. This records a historical spelling association between 哥 and 歌/謌; it does not establish that 哥 originally meant ‘sing’ or that 歌 arose by borrowing the entire 哥 graph.
evidence.title: 說文解字「哥」

evidence.source: Wiktionary, Appendix: Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction
evidence.text: The table gives modern Mandarin gē (Pinyin), Middle Chinese ka in the page’s romanization, and Baxter–Sagart (2014) Old Chinese *[k]ˤaj for 歌. These are readings and a reconstruction for 歌, not directly recorded ancient pronunciations.
evidence.title: Appendix:Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction - Wiktionary

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 歌 character entry; Zhengzhang phonetic-series table
evidence.text: The inspected character page lists 歌 and 哥 together at Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese *kaːl and gives 歌 Baxter–Sagart (2014) *[k]ˤaj. The matching *kaːl forms in one reconstruction system support the traditional phonetic analysis of 哥 in 歌. Do not compare Zhengzhang *kaːl with Baxter–Sagart *[k]ˤaj as though they were a single system; this page did not provide equivalent Baxter–Sagart data for 哥.
evidence.title: 歌 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry quotes the Shuowen analysis and cites 《詩經·魏風·園有桃》 for singing, 《書經·舜典》 for song as lengthened utterance, and later texts for praise and song forms. These are dictionary citations, not dated physical attestations of the graph. The page does not date composition of the cited poem or show when the later senses developed.
evidence.title: 歌 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.text: The entry cites the Shijing line ‘心之憂矣，我歌且謠’ and the Shujing phrase ‘詩言志，歌永言,’ and records senses including singing, praising, musical song and a singable verse genre. These citations show textual uses, but the dictionary gloss order cannot be used as a semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 歌 gē - 汉典

evidence.text: The file is described as a digital vector depicting 歌 in the Shuowen seal-script style; Commons identifies the underlying file name as 歌-seal-s06293.svg and indicates public-domain reuse. This is a modern redraw of a dictionary form, not a photograph or facsimile of an ancient artifact.
evidence.title: File:歌-seal.svg - Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: database scope and glyph reuse notice
evidence.text: The official guide describes Xiaoxuetang as a research database covering oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, seal and regular-script forms, among other resources. It states that glyph images and glyph-attribute information obtained through the query interface are offered under CC0 1.0. The live form-evolution record was accessible as a page but supplied no inspectable form labels or image candidates through this browser, so no Xiaoxuetang glyph is selected here.
evidence.title: 小學堂新手入門

gaps: The late Spring-and-Autumn bronze and Warring States forms are reported by a secondary collation; their artifact images and readings were not independently checked against primary facsimiles.

The relation between the reported early 言+可 structure and the received 欠+哥 form remains uncertain. It could reflect chronological change, a variant spelling, or a related form; the available evidence does not justify choosing among these.
The earliest secure physical attestation of 歌 and the date of a surviving witness to its early textual use remain unresolved. Shijing citations do not by themselves date the extant written graph.
The citation sequence does not establish the semantic chronology or pathways for singing, song, praise, and verse-genre senses.

The possible Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison with Burmese ka ‘dance’ was not independently verified with a primary comparative source or dated Burmese evidence; it is separate from the graph’s formation.

No whole-graph borrowing account for 歌 is supported by the inspected sources. Shuowen’s note that 哥 could be used to write 謌/歌 concerns spelling practice and does not prove the origin of 歌 as a graph loan.
The Xiaoxuetang page could be opened, and its guide confirmed the official CC0 notice, but this browser did not expose its form labels or images. No Xiaoxuetang candidate was selected.
No direct reusable image of the reported bronze inscription was established, so the selected Commons candidate is a modern redraw of the received Shuowen seal form, not an ancient artifact image.

items.period: Received Shuowen seal-script form; the depicted form is a modern vector redraw, not a dated artifact
items.caption: A modern redraw of the 歌 form labeled as Shuowen seal script. In the received dictionary analysis, 欠 is the semantic classifier and 哥 supplies the sound; the picture illustrates that received form, not an excavated inscription.
items.alt: A black seal-script style drawing of 歌 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: The Commons description explicitly identifies the form as 歌 in Shuowen seal-script style and states public-domain reuse; it illustrates the received 欠+哥 analysis. Its modern redraw status is made explicit.
items.rights: Public domain as stated on the Commons file description page.

limitations.text: The selected image is a modern vector redraw of a dictionary seal form, not a photograph or facsimile of an ancient artifact. No visually verified bronze inscription image was available in this research.
The Xiaoxuetang query page exposed no usable labeled glyph candidate through this browser; its general rights notice alone is not evidence for any particular form.
